explanation:
[EFFECT] Higher wind speeds consistently reduce predicted bike rentals, with the effect becoming more pronounced as winds strengthen. At low wind speeds (near calm), the contribution is close to zero — meaning little impact on demand. As wind speed rises beyond roughly 0.3 (about 20 km/h), contributions turn increasingly negative, and at the highest observed speeds (around 0.8–0.9, or ~55–60 km/h) the model predicts a substantial drop in rentals.

[IMPORTANCE] Windspeed is the second-least important feature in the model, ranked 8th out of 9, with an importance score of 0.020. It plays only a minor role in shaping predicted demand compared to factors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because wind has a real but modest effect, it is worth monitoring forecasts for unusually high-wind days (above ~20 km/h) as a signal to slightly reduce bike availability or staff levels, particularly at exposed docking stations.
